messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On‑prem inference deployment — handoff, network walkthrough, and checklist

Hi Alice / Bryan —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for your on‑prem inference rollout. This thread is the handoff & network walkthrough so we can align on control‑plane/data‑plane boundaries, egress/audit expectations, and the ops checklist we need to complete before the cutover.

Agenda (15–30m walkthrough + 30m Q&A):
- Quick architecture overview: control plane (Redwood agents + control API) vs data plane (model serving pools)
- Network requirements: peering, NAT/Egress IPs, firewall rules, MTLS endpoints
- Audit & log flow: retention windows, S3/ELK endpoints, SOC2 evidence items you requested
- Runbook & handoff checklist: cutover steps, rollback, cert rotation cadence
- Open items / timeline / owners

Attachments: onprem‑inference‑reference.pdf (reference diagrams), controlplane‑dataplane‑schematic.png, deploy‑handoff‑runbook.md — please skim the diagrams before our call.

Questions for you before the meeting:
1) Do you have a preferred time window for peering (we need a 2‑hour maintenance window for initial config)?
2) Are there existing NAT IPs you want us to use, or should we provide an expected SNAT range?
3) For audit logs: retention minimum is 90 days by default — do you need longer?

Proposed times (PST): Tue 2026‑07‑20 10:00 or Wed 2026‑07‑21 14:00. I’ll lock the 21st 14:00 slot unless you prefer otherwise.

Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough.

—
Logan Wright
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0128

Logan —

Thanks, this looks great. Wed 07/21 at 14:00 PST works for us. A couple quick clarifications before the call so we can prep our network team: 

- Egress IPs: We need a static SNAT block for outbound calls so our vendor firewall rules can be locked down. Can you provide the expected /28 (or similar) range you’ll use for model telemetry and health pings?
- Audit logging: We will need 1 year retention for audit logs for our compliance team. Is that configurable on your side or do we need to forward logs to our S3?
- Control plane endpoints: will those be reachable over an internal peering connection only, or do we need to open additional inbound ports from the public internet?

Also looping Bryan who will drive the peering/ops side on our side. He might invite CloudOps support to the call if we need firewall rule walkthrough.

Thanks,
Alice
Director of Data Platform, Acme Media

Hi Alice / Bryan —

Quick answers ahead of tomorrow’s session (will deep‑dive on call):

1) SNAT/Egress ranges
- We can provide a recommended public SNAT block as a single /28 for the initial rollout. Suggested allocation: 52.120.34.0/28 (placeholder — final allocation will be assigned by our infra team and coordinated with your firewall admin). Please treat this as informational until we confirm assignment.

2) Audit logging / retention
- Redwood can forward audit and access logs to customer‑owned S3 buckets via an encrypted transfer role. If you need 1 year retention, we recommend forwarding to your S3 (we keep 90 days on our side for quick access and 1 year is supported externally). We’ll include the S3 ingestion IAM policy in the runbook.

3) Control plane reachability
- Control plane API (agent registration, rollout control) should be reachable over the private peering/VPC‑peer. No public inbound ports required if you accept our peering. For on‑prem sites where peering is not available, we offer a TLS egress tunnel option that uses mutual TLS to our control endpoint over standard outbound 443.

Network checklist highlights (we’ll walk this during the call):
- Accept peering and BGP/route propagation windows (2h planned maintenance)
- Firewall rules: allow HTTPS outbound to control plane CIDRs, allow inter‑subnet connectivity between model pools and KV cache endpoints
- NAT/SNAT assignment and test IPs for telemetry/health checks
- TLS certs: we recommend short‑lived cert rotation (90 days) for agent identities; we’ll provide a cert rotation helper script in the runbook
- Egress filtering: list of domains IPs for ES/metrics/telemetry (we’ll provide final list)

Attached I’ve dropped the controlplane‑dataplane‑schematic.png and the handoff runbook draft (deploy‑handoff‑runbook.md). Diego and Irene are owning the runbook pieces: Diego will validate data plane prerequisites (GPU node labels, kernel versions, docker runtime flags), Irene will own audit/log delivery and LMS onboarding.

Action items before call:
- Bryan / Acme: confirm who will accept the peering and provide contact for your firewall admin (name + email).
- Acme: confirm whether you want us to propose the SNAT block or if you’ll provide public IPs.
- Redwood (Diego): send a short kernel/runtime compatibility checklist for model serving pools.

We’ll cover all of this at Wed 14:00 PST — invite is on the calendar.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
